Pieter van Musschenbroek, qui s'en est p: Pieter van Musschenbroek, who got a shock from it, wrote that he would not take another for the kingdom of France.
Un courant électrique fait dévier une bo: An electric current deflects a compass.
Hans Christian Ørsted remarque, pendant: During a lecture, Hans Christian Ørsted notices that a wire carrying a current moves a compass needle: electricity and magnetism are linked.
Georg Ohm relie tension, courant et rési: Georg Ohm links voltage, current and resistance.
Son travail est d'abord si mal reçu qu'O: His work was at first so badly received that Ohm lost his teaching post. He was recognized by the Royal Society in 1841.
Edison réussit son premier essai d'ampou: Edison succeeds in his first test of a carbon-filament bulb.
Joseph Swan avait présenté une ampoule à: Joseph Swan had presented a bulb in Newcastle a few months earlier. The two men ended up joining forces.
Edison ouvre à New York, à Pearl Street,: Edison opens his first commercial power station at Pearl Street, in New York.
Le 4 septembre 1882, elle alimente envir: On September 4, 1882, it powers about 400 lamps for 85 customers in the Wall Street district, with direct current.
Heinrich Hertz produit et détecte des on: Heinrich Hertz produces and detects radio waves in the laboratory.
Il confirme Maxwell. Interrogé sur l'uti: He confirms Maxwell. Asked what his discovery was good for, he is said to have answered: “Nothing.” The unit of frequency bears his name.
Claude Shannon montre que des circuits d: Claude Shannon shows that relay circuits can perform logic.
Son mémoire de master au MIT, à 21 ans,: His master's thesis at MIT, at 21, links Boolean algebra to circuits. It has been called the most important master's thesis of the century.
Aux laboratoires Bell, Bardeen et Bratta: At Bell Labs, Bardeen and Brattain get the first transistor working.
Le 16 décembre 1947, un morceau de germa: On December 16, 1947, a piece of germanium and a gold contact amplify a signal. William Shockley, their boss, improves the device right after.
Une pile de disques de zinc et de cuivre: A stack of zinc and copper discs gives the first continuous current.
Alessandro Volta la décrit dans une lett: Alessandro Volta described it in a letter to the Royal Society, on 20 March 1800. The same year, it was used to decompose water.
Un étudiant de Königsberg écrit les deux: A Königsberg student writes the two rules that make it possible to calculate every circuit.
À Königsberg, Gustav Kirchhoff énonce la: In Königsberg, Gustav Kirchhoff stated the junction rule and the loop rule. They generalise Ohm's law to any network.
Dans une forge du New Jersey, un fil d'e: In a New Jersey ironworks, a two-mile wire transmits a proverb.
Le 6 janvier 1838, à Speedwell, Alfred V: On 6 January 1838, at Speedwell, Alfred Vail and Samuel Morse sent "A patient waiter is no loser". Six years later, the Washington-Baltimore line opened.
À Rome, un médecin de l'empereur soigne: In Rome, an imperial physician treats migraine with an electric fish.
Scribonius Largus, médecin de Claude, re: Scribonius Largus, Claudius's physician, recommends the torpedo's shock against headaches and gout. The fish's name comes from torpere, "to be numb".
À Milet, un philosophe frotte un morceau: In Miletus, a philosopher rubs a piece of amber, and straw starts to move.
Thalès croit à un effet magnétique ; c'e: Thales believes it is a magnetic effect; it is static electricity. From amber, ēlektron in Greek, would come the word electricity.
Par temps couvert, les marins chinois re: In dark weather, Chinese sailors look at the south-pointing needle.
Zhu Yu le note dans ses Propos de table: Zhu Yu noted it in his Pingzhou Table Talks, written between 1111 and 1117. It is the first attested use of the compass at sea.
Un Picard écrit à un soldat ce que perso: A Picard writes to a soldier what nobody had written: the magnet has two poles.
Pierre de Maricourt date sa lettre du 8: Peter of Maricourt dated his letter 8 August 1269. He also described in it the first pivoted compass.
Un médecin de Londres promène une aiguil: A London physician moves a needle over a small lodestone ball, and understands the compass.
William Gilbert publie De Magnete en 160: William Gilbert published De Magnete in 1600. In it he also coined the Latin word electricus, "like amber".
Un imprimeur et son fils font voler une: A printer and his son fly a key under a storm.
En juin 1752, à Philadelphie, Franklin c: In June 1752, in Philadelphia, Franklin charged a Leyden jar with a kite. A month earlier, Dalibard had succeeded with the rod experiment in France.
Avec un fil qui se tord, un ingénieur pè: With a wire that twists, an engineer weighs the force between two charges.
Charles-Augustin Coulomb publie en 1785: Charles-Augustin Coulomb published in 1785 that the electric force varies as the inverse square of the distance. Doubling the distance divides the force by four.
À Cambridge, on découvre la première par: In Cambridge, the first particle smaller than an atom is discovered.
Le 30 avril 1897, J. J. Thomson annonce: On 30 April 1897, J. J. Thomson announced that cathode rays are made of negatively charged "corpuscles". They would be called electrons.
À 4,2 degrés du zéro absolu, le mercure: At 4.2 degrees above absolute zero, mercury lets current through without the slightest loss.
Le 8 avril 1911, à Leyde, Heike Kamerlin: On 8 April 1911, in Leiden, Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered superconductivity. Nobel Prize in 1913.
